summary: Polyvinyl alcohol is a polymeric ocular lubricant (demulcent) used as an over-the-counter artificial tear to relieve dryness and minor irritation of the eye, including discomfort from exposure to wind or sun. It works physically by coating the ocular surface to retain moisture and reduce friction; it has no pharmacologic systemic action. It is often combined with other demulcents such as povidone. The usual use is 1-2 drops in the affected eye(s) as needed. It is for external (ophthalmic) use only. Patients should stop and consult a clinician if they have eye pain, vision changes, continued redness or irritation, or if symptoms persist or worsen.

moa: Polyvinyl alcohol is an inert, water-soluble synthetic polymer that acts as an ocular demulcent. Applied topically, it increases the viscosity and stability of the tear film, coats and lubricates the ocular surface, retains moisture, and reduces friction and irritation. The effect is purely physical/protective; there is no systemic pharmacologic activity.

preg: Polyvinyl alcohol is a topical ophthalmic lubricant with negligible systemic absorption and no systemic pharmacologic activity; it is generally considered low risk in pregnancy. As with any product, use during pregnancy after discussing with a clinician if there are concerns.
lact: As a topical ocular lubricant with negligible systemic absorption, polyvinyl alcohol is generally considered compatible with breastfeeding.
renal: Not applicable. There is no clinically meaningful systemic absorption of a topical ocular lubricant, so no renal considerations apply.
hepatic: Not applicable. There is no clinically meaningful systemic absorption, so no hepatic considerations apply.

pearls: An OTC ocular demulcent (artificial tear) that works physically to lubricate and stabilize the tear film - no systemic pharmacology
Frequently combined with povidone or other demulcents in lubricant eye drops
Use 1-2 drops as needed; for ophthalmic (external) use only
Eye pain, vision change, or persistent redness warrants professional evaluation rather than continued self-treatment
Negligible systemic absorption means it is generally safe across renal/hepatic impairment, pregnancy, and lactation
missed: There is no fixed dosing schedule - polyvinyl alcohol eye drops are used as needed for symptom relief, so there is no missed dose to make up.
overdose: Overdose is not expected with topical ocular use. Accidental ingestion of small amounts is generally of low toxicity; provide supportive care and contact a poison control center if a large amount is ingested. Excess drops simply overflow the eye and can be wiped away.
